title: Where are you from?
description: A guided 45–60 minute lesson distinguishing nationality, country or place of origin, current residence and hometown roots. Ask and answer each question naturally in Northern Vietnamese.
teacher_intro: Welcome to Lesson 6. In Lesson 5 you learned to introduce yourself. Today we will make your introduction more precise by distinguishing where you come from, where you live now, and your quê — your home place or roots. Allow 45–60 minutes. Follow the method: listen to the English teacher, think, pause and speak aloud, then compare with the student voices. Use the neutral classroom pronoun tôi for yourself and bạn for a peer. In real conversation, pronouns and forms of address depend on age, relationship and setting.
background: This lesson develops three related but different Vietnamese patterns. Tôi đến từ… means 'I come from…' and answers Bạn đến từ đâu? ('Where do you come from?'). Tôi sống ở… means 'I live in…' and answers Bạn sống ở đâu? ('Where do you live?'). Quê bạn ở đâu? asks about someone's home place, hometown or roots; a simple answer is Quê tôi ở… . The word quê can refer to a village, town, province, region or broader homeland depending on context. Quốc tịch means nationality. Tôi là người Tanzania identifies nationality, while Tôi đến từ Tanzania states origin. Tôi sống ở Úc states current residence. Người means person; đến từ means come from; sống ở means live in/at; đâu means where; quê means home place or roots; nhưng means but; và means and. The usual Vietnamese name for Australia is Úc. Place and city names can remain proper names inside these sentence patterns.
culture: A person's nationality, birthplace, family roots, hometown and current residence may all be different. Vietnamese speakers may ask Bạn đến từ đâu? to ask where someone comes from, or Quê bạn ở đâu? to learn about the person's home place or roots. Quê is not always a simple synonym for country: it may refer to a village, town or province, and some people have more than one meaningful connection. Do not assume that a person's current city is their quê. Let the speaker explain. This lesson uses bạn as a classroom peer pronoun, but real Vietnamese address terms depend on age, familiarity and relationship. A short, clear answer is usually enough; you do not need to give a full biography immediately.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Welcome to Lesson 6. In Lesson 5 you learned to introduce yourself: your name, nationality, country of origin and where you live. Today we will make one part of that introduction more precise: where you are from.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Isn’t that the same as saying my nationality or the country I come from?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Sometimes, but not always. Someone may be Tanzanian, have grown up in Tanzania, come from a particular town, and now live in Australia. Those are related facts, but they are not identical.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Our method remains Think, Speak, Reveal, Compare. I will explain a small pattern. Pause and build your answer aloud before the student voices respond.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: So I should try to make the Vietnamese sentence myself instead of waiting to copy it.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. Keep the tones and vowel marks clear. We are using contemporary Northern Vietnamese with a Hanoi reference accent.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: First, review the question Bạn đến từ đâu? It means Where do you come from? Listen to the parts: bạn — you; đến — come or arrive; từ — from; đâu — where.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Say it again as one complete question. Keep đâu with its rising tone.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — slow model: Bạn đến từ đâu? Pause. Repeat at a natural conversational pace. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now answer with Tôi đến từ… followed by a place. For example: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Correct. The pattern is reusable. Replace the country with another place name when needed.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let us separate three ideas. Quốc tịch means nationality. Đến từ asks where someone comes from. Sống ở asks where someone lives now.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: So if I am Tanzanian but live in Australia, I can say Tôi là người Tanzania, nhưng tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. And if someone asks where you come from, you can answer Tôi đến từ Tanzania. These sentences answer different questions.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Build the nationality sentence: I am a Tanzanian person.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi là người Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now build the origin sentence: I come from Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now build the residence sentence: I live in Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Join the three ideas. Use nhưng — but — to show the contrast between origin and present residence.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi là người Tanzania. Tôi đến từ Tanzania, nhưng tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — three separate sentences, then the connected version, first slowly and then naturally. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now we will learn another useful question: Bạn sống ở đâu? Where do you live?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. The answer is Tôi sống ở… followed by the place.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Notice that you do not add là. Tôi sống ở Úc is already a complete sentence.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Ask me where I live. Use bạn as the classroom peer pronoun.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now answer with a place you know. Try: I live in Sydney.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Sydney.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. City names are proper names. Keep the Vietnamese sentence frame and insert the place name.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A different question is Quê bạn ở đâu? This asks about someone's home place or hometown background. Quê means homeland, home place or native place, depending on context.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Is that exactly the same as Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Not exactly. Bạn đến từ đâu? can ask where someone comes from, including a country or place. Quê bạn ở đâu? often asks about family roots or the place someone considers their hometown.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Listen to the question: Quê bạn ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Quê bạn ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A simple answer is Quê tôi ở… — My home place is in… Another possible answer is Tôi quê ở… in suitable conversational contexts. For now, practise the clear pattern Quê tôi ở…

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Quê tôi ở Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: That is a practice example. If your hometown is a particular city or region, name that place instead.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — Quê bạn ở đâu? Quê tôi ở… Record a careful version and a natural conversational version. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let us compare the questions side by side. Bạn đến từ đâu? asks where you come from. Bạn sống ở đâu? asks where you live. Quê bạn ở đâu? asks about your home place or roots.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: They all contain a place, but the meaning is different.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. Do not answer automatically with the same sentence every time. First understand what the speaker is asking.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: I will ask three questions. Answer each one with a matching sentence. First: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Second: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Third: Quê bạn ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Quê tôi ở Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. These answers can all be true about one person. They describe origin, current residence and home roots.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now practise asking another person. Use Bạn đến từ đâu? and then return the question with Còn bạn? — And you?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Việt Nam. Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Now answer with your own information. Use a country or city that is true for you.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania. Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Remember that these are sample roles. Change the places to match the real speaker. Do not memorise a false biography.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A short note about place names: Việt Nam is Vietnam; Úc is the usual Vietnamese name for Australia; Tanzania is commonly used as the country name Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Should I translate every city name into Vietnamese?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: No. Many city and place names are used as proper names. Keep the name recognisable and pronounce it as clearly as you can. The sentence pattern carries the grammar.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Say: I come from Tanzania, but I live in Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania, nhưng tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now say: My home place is in Tanzania, and I live in Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Quê tôi ở Tanzania, và tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Và means and. Nhưng means but. Choose the connector that matches the relationship between the ideas.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now let us build a longer introduction. Begin with Xin chào. Add your name: Tên tôi là… or Tôi tên là…

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Tên tôi là Jeremiah.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Next say your nationality: Tôi là người Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi là người Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Then say where you come from: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Finally say where you live now: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Put the information together naturally. You can use separate short sentences. You do not need to force everything into one long sentence.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — model introduction: Xin chào. Tên tôi là Jeremiah. Tôi là người Tanzania. Tôi đến từ Tanzania, nhưng tôi sống ở Úc. Slow version, then natural version. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now listen to a two-person exchange. Person A asks where B comes from. B answers and asks the question back.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Việt Nam. Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania, nhưng tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Now add the question about current residence.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Sydney.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Notice how the conversation moves from origin to present residence. The question tells you which answer is relevant.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let us work on common mistakes. First, do not confuse đến từ with sống ở. Đến từ is come from; sống ở is live in.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: If I say Tôi sống ở Tanzania, I am saying I live in Tanzania, not that I come from there.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Correct. Second, do not insert là into every sentence. Tôi là người Tanzania identifies what kind of person you are. Tôi sống ở Úc does not need là.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Correct this sentence: Tôi là sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. Now correct this one if the intended meaning is I am Tanzanian: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi là người Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. The original sentence means I come from Tanzania. It is grammatical, but it answers a different question.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A little cultural context: in Vietnamese, asking about quê can be a way of learning someone's roots. It may refer to a village, town, province or broader home region, not only a country.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: So someone who lives in Hanoi might have quê in another province.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. A person's current address and quê may be different. Some people have moved many times, and some identify with more than one place.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Do not assume that every person has one simple hometown answer. Listen to the wording and let the speaker explain.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: And if I only want to ask which country someone comes from, Bạn đến từ đâu? is a useful beginner question.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Yes. It is a clear, general question. Relationship-sensitive pronouns still matter in real conversations; bạn is our classroom practice form.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now practise a quick response drill. I will give the English meaning. Pause and say the Vietnamese before the student answers. I come from Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: I live in Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Where do you come from?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Where do you live?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Where is your home place?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Quê bạn ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: My home place is in Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Quê tôi ở Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Repeat any phrase that required extra thought.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now add a polite greeting and a natural ending. Start: Xin chào. Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania. Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Việt Nam.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask where the other person lives.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Hà Nội.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Finish with a simple thanks and goodbye if the conversation is ending.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn. Tạm biệt!

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — full exchange with two speakers, conversational rhythm and clear Northern pronunciation. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Final challenge. Without reading, introduce yourself with your name, nationality, country of origin and current place of residence.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Tên tôi là Jeremiah. Tôi là người Tanzania. Tôi đến từ Tanzania, nhưng tôi sống ở Úc.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. You have completed Lesson 6. Keep the three questions separate in your mind, and practise answering with places that are true for you.

title: Polite words
description: A guided 45–60 minute lesson on thanking, apologising, getting attention, asking permission, requesting help and asking someone to repeat or explain. Practise complete, natural Northern Vietnamese exchanges.
teacher_intro: Welcome to Lesson 7. Today you will learn to thank people, apologise, get someone's attention, ask for help, ask someone to repeat something and respond politely. Allow 45–60 minutes. Follow Think, Speak, Reveal, Compare: listen to the explanation, pause and answer aloud before comparing with the student voices. We use bạn and tôi as classroom defaults; real Vietnamese address terms depend on age, relationship and setting.
background: Cảm ơn means thank you. Cảm ơn nhiều adds emphasis: thanks a lot. Không có gì is a common response to thanks, similar to you're welcome or it's nothing. Xin lỗi means sorry and can also politely attract someone's attention. Không sao reassures someone after an apology: it's okay or no problem. Làm ơn introduces a request, as in Làm ơn giúp tôi (Please help me). Xin phép signals asking permission or politely excusing yourself. Useful complete request patterns include Bạn có thể… không? (Can you…?) and Bạn có thể… được không? (Could you…?). Chưa means not yet; nói lại means say again; giải thích means explain; chậm hơn means more slowly; một chút means a little. Cho tôi… can introduce a request for an item. The exact choice of expression depends on context, tone and the relationship between speakers.
culture: Vietnamese politeness is not carried by one word equivalent to English please. It is expressed through word choice, tone, the structure of a request and especially the way speakers address one another. Bạn is a useful classroom peer pronoun, but it is not a universal form of address. Vietnamese speakers commonly choose relationship terms such as anh, chị, em, cô, chú or bác according to age, familiarity and social relationship. Cảm ơn and xin lỗi are widely useful, but do not assume every English use of please, excuse me or you're welcome maps to one Vietnamese expression. Không có gì commonly responds to thanks; không sao commonly reassures after an apology. Làm ơn can sound direct if used without a suitable tone or context, so practise it as part of a complete courteous request. Observe how people around you speak and adapt your address terms to the situation.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Welcome to Lesson 7. Today you will learn to thank people, apologise, get someone's attention, ask for help, ask someone to repeat something and respond politely. Allow 45–60 minutes. Our method is Think, Speak, Reveal, Compare: listen, pause, answer aloud, then compare.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: I know cảm ơn and xin lỗi. Are those the main polite words?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: They are two essential expressions, but politeness also depends on your tone, the situation and the way you address the other person. We will build useful complete sentences, not just memorise isolated words.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: First expression: cảm ơn — thank you. Listen to both syllables: cảm ơn. Keep the written tone marks in mind.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Say it again clearly, without rushing the two syllables.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — cảm ơn. First say it slowly, then naturally, then repeat it three times. Actual audio recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You can make your thanks a little stronger with nhiều: cảm ơn nhiều — thank you very much / thanks a lot.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn nhiều.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Another useful expression is cảm ơn bạn — thank you. Here bạn is the classroom word for you.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn bạn.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now imagine someone thanks you. A common response is không có gì — you're welcome / it's nothing.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không có gì.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Listen to the difference in meaning. Không có gì is a natural response to thanks. Không sao often means it's okay or no problem, especially after an apology.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: So I should not use them as if they were exactly the same.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Correct. Practise the exchange. I say cảm ơn bạn. You respond.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không có gì.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now reverse the roles. Thank your partner.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn bạn.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không có gì.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. In a real conversation, the relationship pronouns may change. For now, bạn is our consistent classroom choice.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Our second key expression is xin lỗi. It can mean sorry, and it can also politely get someone's attention, similar to excuse me.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Repeat it slowly. Notice the hỏi tone mark in lỗi.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — xin lỗi. Record a careful version and a natural conversational version. Then model it as an apology and as a polite attention-getter. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: If you accidentally bump into someone, you can say xin lỗi. The other person may reassure you with không sao — it's okay / no problem.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không sao.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Now say: Sorry, I'm late. Use xin lỗi and tôi đến muộn.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, tôi đến muộn.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: That is a useful complete sentence. Đến muộn means to arrive late.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Try another apology: Sorry, I don't understand. Tôi chưa hiểu means I don't understand yet.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, tôi chưa hiểu.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Chưa means not yet. This is a useful way to explain a difficulty without pretending you understood.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now let's get someone's attention politely. Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi… means Excuse me, may I ask…

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi…

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Cho tôi hỏi literally introduces a question you would like to ask. It is a useful phrase before asking for directions or information.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi, nhà vệ sinh ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. That means Excuse me, may I ask, where is the toilet? Nhà vệ sinh is a common polite term for toilet or restroom.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi, nhà vệ sinh ở đâu? Model it as one smooth polite question, first slowly and then naturally. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now requests. Làm ơn is a polite request expression similar to please. A simple example is làm ơn giúp tôi — please help me.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Làm ơn giúp tôi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. This is clear and direct. Help is giúp; tôi is me / I in this classroom pattern.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You can also put the request into a question: Bạn có thể giúp tôi không? — Can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể giúp tôi không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Có thể means can or be able to. Không at the end makes this a yes-or-no question.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: So the shape is Bạn có thể… không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. Try: Can you speak more slowly? The sentence is Bạn có thể nói chậm hơn không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể nói chậm hơn không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Nói is speak; chậm hơn is more slowly. This sentence is especially useful when learning a language.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A slightly fuller version is Bạn có thể nói chậm hơn một chút được không? — Could you speak a little more slowly?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể nói chậm hơn một chút được không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Một chút means a little. Được không is another way to ask whether something is possible or acceptable. Learn this as a complete polite request.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask someone to repeat something: Bạn có thể nói lại được không? — Could you say that again?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể nói lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Lại means again in this expression. You can also say Bạn nói lại được không? in a shorter conversational form.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn nói lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now combine the expressions: Xin lỗi, bạn có thể nói lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, bạn có thể nói lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. You have used xin lỗi to soften the request, then asked the person to repeat.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Another useful phrase is Tôi không hiểu — I don't understand. But Tôi chưa hiểu — I don't understand yet — can sound more open to further explanation.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi chưa hiểu. Bạn có thể giải thích lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Giải thích means explain. The full question asks whether the person can explain again.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let's practise asking for something. Cho tôi… means give me… or let me have… depending on context. Add the item after it.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Cho tôi nước, please?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: For a natural Vietnamese request, you can say Cho tôi nước, làm ơn. In a café, you may hear or use Cho tôi một cốc nước — give me a glass of water, please. The setting and tone matter.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cho tôi một cốc nước, làm ơn.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Một cốc nước means a glass of water. Remember that a bare request can sound direct, so use a friendly tone and an appropriate address term.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Another useful request is Bạn có thể cho tôi biết… không? — Could you tell me…?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể cho tôi biết nhà vệ sinh ở đâu không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. That means Could you tell me where the toilet is? It is a longer but very practical question.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — Bạn có thể cho tôi biết nhà vệ sinh ở đâu không? Speak in a calm, courteous tone. Actual recording is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now we will look at xin phép. Xin phép is used when asking permission or politely excusing yourself before doing something.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin phép.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: For example, Xin phép, tôi đi trước nhé means Excuse me, I'll leave first, okay? This is a useful expression when leaving a gathering.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin phép, tôi đi trước nhé.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Nhé can soften a statement or invite agreement, depending on context. Here it makes the announcement feel conversational.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You may also hear Xin phép tôi… when someone is asking permission to do something. Listen for the phrase as a polite signal.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: So xin lỗi is sorry or excuse me, while xin phép is asking permission or excusing myself.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: That is a useful first distinction. They can overlap in English translation, but their usual functions are different.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Politeness also comes from address terms. Bạn is useful between peers, but Vietnamese speakers often choose anh, chị, em, cô, chú or bác according to age and relationship.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Does that mean I should not call everyone bạn?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Correct. Bạn is our classroom default, not a universal word for every person in every situation. Observe how people address one another, and follow the relationship that fits.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: For a simple practice exchange, keep using bạn. Say thank you to a classmate.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn bạn.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không có gì.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now apologise for arriving late.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, tôi đến muộn.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không sao.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask for help.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể giúp tôi không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Được. Tôi giúp bạn.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Được means okay / can do. Tôi giúp bạn means I will help you.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask someone to speak more slowly.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, bạn có thể nói chậm hơn một chút được không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Được, tôi sẽ nói chậm hơn.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Tôi sẽ nói chậm hơn means I will speak more slowly. Sẽ marks a future action.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let's do a listening-and-response drill. I will give the situation in English. Think first, then say the Vietnamese phrase aloud.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Situation one: Someone gives you directions. You want to say thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn nhiều.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Situation two: You accidentally interrupt someone. Get their attention politely before asking a question.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi…

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Situation three: You did not hear the last sentence. Ask the person to repeat it.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, bạn có thể nói lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Situation four: Someone apologises for a small mistake. Reassure them.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Không sao.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Situation five: You need assistance carrying something. Ask politely.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn có thể giúp tôi không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Situation six: You are leaving before the others. Excuse yourself politely.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin phép, tôi đi trước nhé.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now compare the core expressions. Cảm ơn expresses thanks. Xin lỗi apologises or gets attention. Không sao reassures after an apology. Không có gì responds to thanks. Làm ơn introduces a request. Xin phép signals permission or excusing yourself.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: The English translations sometimes overlap, so I need to remember the situation.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. Context is part of meaning. Do not translate each phrase mechanically.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let's build a short conversation in a public place. One person needs help finding the restroom.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi, nhà vệ sinh ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Nhà vệ sinh ở bên kia.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Bên kia means over there / on the other side. The answer is a simple direction.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn bạn nhiều.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Không có gì.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now imagine you did not understand the direction. Ask for it again.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, tôi chưa hiểu. Bạn có thể nói lại được không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Được. Nhà vệ sinh ở bên kia.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. This is a complete practical exchange: attract attention, explain the difficulty, ask for repetition and thank the person.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording script — full public-place dialogue. Record each line separately, then the complete exchange at natural speed. Actual audio is not included.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Final speaking challenge. Without looking at the cards, say: thank you; you're welcome; sorry; no problem; please help me; could you repeat that; and excuse me, may I ask?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn. Không có gì. Xin lỗi. Không sao. Làm ơn giúp tôi. Bạn có thể nói lại được không? Xin lỗi, cho tôi hỏi…

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. Finish by creating your own short conversation. Include one thank-you, one apology or attention-getter, and one polite request. Use bạn for the classroom partner, and speak with a calm, friendly tone.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin lỗi, bạn có thể giúp tôi không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Được. Tôi giúp bạn.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Cảm ơn bạn nhiều.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Không có gì.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: That completes Lesson 7. Review the expressions aloud tomorrow, especially the difference between không có gì and không sao. In Lesson 8, we will learn numbers from zero to twenty and use them in simple questions.

title: Numbers 0–20
description: A 45–60 minute guided lesson counting from zero to twenty, recognising numbers in random order, using the special form mười lăm, and asking and answering simple quantity questions.
teacher_intro: Welcome to Lesson 8: Numbers 0–20. Allow 45–60 minutes. Learn the numbers with their tones, practise the full sequence forwards and backwards, then use them with simple quantities. Follow Think, Speak, Reveal, Compare: pause before the student voices answer and say each number aloud.
background: The numbers from zero to ten are không, một, hai, ba, bốn, năm, sáu, bảy, tám, chín, mười. Eleven to nineteen generally follow mười + the unit number: mười một, mười hai, mười ba, mười bốn, mười lăm, mười sáu, mười bảy, mười tám, mười chín. Fifteen is the special form mười lăm, not mười năm. Twenty is hai mươi, literally two tens. Numbers are followed by a classifier and noun where Vietnamese uses one, for example hai quyển sách (two books). Bao nhiêu asks how many or how much. Mấy is also common in questions about small quantities of countable things.
culture: Vietnamese speakers use classifiers between numbers and many nouns. Quyển is used for books: một quyển sách, hai quyển sách. Cái is a common general classifier for many objects, although the appropriate classifier depends on the noun. In the number fifteen, năm changes to lăm: mười lăm. Do not change năm everywhere; five on its own remains năm, as in counting or năm quyển sách. Bao nhiêu is a broadly useful way to ask about quantity or amount; mấy is also common with countable items and often suggests a relatively small number. When giving a phone number, digits are generally spoken one by one. Pronunciation and tone are essential: learn the sound of each number rather than relying on spelling alone.

title: Age and basic details
description: A 45–60 minute lesson on asking and answering age, names, origin, current residence, work and languages, then combining the details in a natural first-meeting introduction.
teacher_intro: Welcome to Lesson 9: Age and basic details. Allow 45–60 minutes. We will ask and answer someone's age, say how old we are, ask simple personal questions and practise giving short answers. Follow Think, Speak, Reveal, Compare: pause and answer before the student voices respond.
background: Tuổi means age or years of age. A simple age question is Bạn bao nhiêu tuổi? and the answer pattern is Tôi + number + tuổi, for example Tôi hai mươi tuổi (I am twenty years old). Vietnamese does not use a separate equivalent of the English verb 'am' in this pattern. Bạn tên là gì? asks someone's name; Tôi tên là… or Tên tôi là… gives it. Bạn sống ở đâu? asks where someone currently lives; Bạn đến từ đâu? asks where they come from. Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia combines origin and current residence. Bạn làm nghề gì? asks about occupation; Bạn nói tiếng gì? asks what language someone speaks. Đang học means is learning; chưa means not yet.
culture: Questions about age and personal details depend on context. Bạn bao nhiêu tuổi? is useful for classroom practice and familiar exchanges, but asking a stranger's age immediately may feel too personal. Vietnamese pronouns and forms of address reflect age, relationship and social context. Bạn is a convenient classroom default, but real speakers may use anh, chị, em, cô, chú, bác or other relationship terms. Distinguish origin (đến từ) from current residence (sống ở) and workplace (làm việc ở). These are different facts and should be answered with the matching phrase. Học sinh generally refers to school pupils, while sinh viên generally refers to university or college students. Treat the sample names, ages and locations as practice examples rather than personal information that must be shared.

dialogue.line: Bạn tên là gì?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A simple answer is Tôi tên là… — My name is…

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi tên là An.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. You can also say Tên tôi là An. Both patterns are useful.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tên tôi là An.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask where someone lives: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Answer: Tôi sống ở Australia — I live in Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Australia.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Sống means live; ở introduces the place in this sentence.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask where someone comes from: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Answer: Tôi đến từ Tanzania — I come from Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Keep the difference clear: đến từ asks about origin; sống ở asks where someone lives now.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You can combine the two facts: Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia — I am from Tanzania but live in Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. Nhưng means but. This is a natural way to contrast origin and current residence.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask about someone's work or study. Bạn làm nghề gì? means What do you do for a living?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn làm nghề gì?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A simple answer can be Tôi là giáo viên — I am a teacher. Nghề means profession or occupation.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi là giáo viên.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: If you are a student, you can say Tôi là học sinh or Tôi là sinh viên, depending on the educational context.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi là sinh viên.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Học sinh is generally used for school pupils; sinh viên is generally used for university or college students.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You can also ask Bạn làm việc ở đâu? — Where do you work?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn làm việc ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Answer: Tôi làm việc ở Sydney — I work in Sydney.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi làm việc ở Sydney.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Làm việc means work. This is a different question from Bạn sống ở đâu? — Where do you live?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let's practise a few basic personal details. Bạn có gia đình chưa? can ask whether someone has a family yet, but it may be personal. For this course, we will focus on less sensitive everyday details.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: What other simple details can I ask?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You can ask Bạn nói tiếng gì? — What language do you speak?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn nói tiếng gì?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A simple answer is Tôi nói tiếng Anh — I speak English.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi nói tiếng Anh.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: You can add another language with và, meaning and: Tôi nói tiếng Anh và tiếng Bồ Đào Nha — I speak English and Portuguese.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi nói tiếng Anh và tiếng Bồ Đào Nha.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Tiếng introduces a language name. Tiếng Anh is English; tiếng Việt is Vietnamese; tiếng Bồ Đào Nha is Portuguese.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now ask whether someone speaks Vietnamese: Bạn nói tiếng Việt không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn nói tiếng Việt không?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A positive answer is Có, tôi nói một chút — Yes, I speak a little.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Có, tôi nói một chút.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: A negative answer is Không, tôi chưa nói tiếng Việt tốt — No, I don't speak Vietnamese well yet. Chưa means not yet.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Không, tôi chưa nói tiếng Việt tốt.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. You can also say Tôi đang học tiếng Việt — I am learning Vietnamese. Đang marks an action in progress.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đang học tiếng Việt.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now we will build a short personal introduction. Listen once, then repeat it in sections.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Tôi tên là An. Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia. Tôi nói tiếng Anh và đang học tiếng Việt.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. That introduction gives a name, origin, current residence, a language and something you are learning.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Add age to the introduction: Tôi hai mươi tuổi. Put it after your name if you want.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Tôi tên là An. Tôi hai mươi tuổi. Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. Now make the same introduction with a different age and place.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Tôi tên là Minh. Tôi mười tám tuổi. Tôi sống ở Hà Nội.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Hà Nội is a place name. Remember to pronounce the tones clearly.

dialogue.speaker: NATIVE SPEAKER · NORTHERN VIETNAMESE
dialogue.line: Recording prompt — model the two full introductions at slow teaching speed and natural conversational speed. Leave a pause after each sentence for learners to repeat. Audio has not yet been recorded.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now a question-and-answer drill. Ask: How old are you?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn bao nhiêu tuổi?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi mười chín tuổi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Ask: What is your name?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn tên là gì?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi tên là An.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Ask: Where do you live?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn sống ở đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Australia.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Ask: Where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Ask: What language do you speak?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn nói tiếng gì?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi nói tiếng Anh.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Ask: What do you do?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn làm nghề gì?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi là giáo viên.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now listen to the difference between these three questions: Bạn bao nhiêu tuổi? (How old are you?), Bạn sống ở đâu? (Where do you live?), and Bạn đến từ đâu? (Where are you from?). They ask for different information.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Age, current home and origin.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Exactly. Do not answer all three with the same place or number. Listen to the question word and phrase.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let's practise numbers inside age answers. I will say an age in English. Answer in Vietnamese.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Twenty-one. For now, use the number pattern you know and say tuổi after it.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Hai mươi mốt tuổi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Mốt is used for one in certain numbers after twenty. We will study numbers beyond twenty in a later lesson; for now, learn this age phrase as a useful example.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Twenty-two.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Hai mươi hai tuổi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Twenty-five.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Hai mươi lăm tuổi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. Lăm is used in the five position in this compound number too. We will practise larger numbers in a later lesson.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now practise a polite age question with an older person. Rather than using bạn, you may use an appropriate relationship term such as anh or chị, depending on the person and your relationship. For this exercise, repeat the structure with bạn.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn bao nhiêu tuổi?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Good. In real conversation, choose the form of address carefully. Age and social relationship affect pronoun choice in Vietnamese.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now a mini-dialogue. Student 1 is meeting Student 2 for the first time. Ask the questions naturally, not as a rapid list.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Bạn tên là gì?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi tên là Minh. Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi tên là An.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn bao nhiêu tuổi?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi hai mươi tuổi. Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi mười tám tuổi.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Bạn đến từ đâu?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Việt Nam. Tôi sống ở Hà Nội.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Còn bạn?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Bạn nói tiếng Việt không?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Có, tôi đang học tiếng Việt.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. You have made a first-meeting conversation using greetings, names, age, origin, residence and language learning.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Final challenge. Without reading, introduce yourself in five sentences: your name, age, where you come from, where you live and a language you speak or are learning.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Tôi tên là An. Tôi hai mươi tuổi. Tôi đến từ Tanzania nhưng sống ở Australia. Tôi nói tiếng Anh và đang học tiếng Việt.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Well done. Review the age question and the difference between origin and current residence. Lesson 10 will bring the first-conversation skills together in a review.

title: Review: first conversation
description: Combine greetings, names, origin, residence, numbers and polite expressions.
teacher_intro: This is your first full review. You already have enough building blocks for a short introduction. Listen to the English, pause, and construct the whole Vietnamese sentence before revealing the answer.
background: Vietnamese sentence building often relies on stable word order and small reusable chunks. Review the chunks as complete patterns: tên tôi là…, tôi đến từ…, tôi sống ở…, tôi … tuổi, and bạn … không?
culture: A good first conversation is not a word-for-word translation of English. Choose a suitable way to address the other person, speak clearly, and let the conversation develop naturally rather than forcing every possible detail into the first exchange.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Let's greet someone: Xin chào. Now ask their name: bạn tên là gì?

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Xin chào. Bạn tên là gì?

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Answer with your name: tên tôi là… Now say where you come from: tôi đến từ…

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 2
dialogue.line: Tên tôi là Linh. Tôi đến từ Việt Nam.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Now add where you live and your age. Remember: tôi sống ở… and tôi … tuổi. No là in the age pattern.

dialogue.speaker: STUDENT 1
dialogue.line: Tôi sống ở Hà Nội. Tôi hai mươi tuổi.

dialogue.speaker: TEACHER · ENGLISH
dialogue.line: Excellent. Finish politely with cảm ơn or tạm biệt. You have built a complete beginner conversation from reusable pieces.
